topStory.headline: MSU Denver Faculty Say Online Assessments Have Become Impossible to Validate
topStory.summary:
At Metropolitan State University Denver, faculty are confronting challenges with student assessment in the A.I. age, according to Denver7. Jeff Loats, professor and director of the Center for Teaching, Learning and Design at MSU, stated that if assessments are online, "we don't know how to do that in a valid way."

Sam Jay, MSU's Executive Director of Online Learning, described this as an opportunity to "right the ship" on assessment practices. Vice Provost Shaun Schafer described flipping his journalism class from in-person lectures with online assignments to online lectures with in-person assignments. He anticipates more case studies and "apply this to your life, apply to your community" assignments because these are harder for A.I. to complete authentically.

Schafer acknowledged that it is difficult for instructors to drastically change their teaching methods, and faculty buy-in varies. Some professors allow limited A.I. use while others restrict it entirely, creating a patchwork approach. The challenge of creating definitive guidelines across more than 100 majors at MSU illustrates how institutional responses are still evolving.

stories.headline: Kazakhstan Plans A.I. University Launch for 2026
stories.summary: Kazakhstan will open a dedicated artificial intelligence university in 2026, according to TV BRICS. The initiative represents the country's commitment to developing A.I. expertise and education infrastructure.

stories.headline: Universidad Austral Integrates A.I. Dashboard for Student Assessment
stories.summary: Universidad Austral partnered with Universidad de La Sabana to develop an intelligent dashboard that allows educators and students to interact with A.I. as both teammate and teaching assistant, according to Times Higher Education. The tool provides continuous feedback and helps students develop better judgment in A.I. use.

stories.headline: San Diego Community College District Hosts 'InnovAItion Day' March 20
stories.summary: The San Diego Community College District is holding InnovAItion Day on March 20, bringing together faculty, staff and students to explore responsible A.I. use in education, according to City Times. The event features student-led panels and discussions about A.I.'s role in learning.

stories.headline: UNC Greensboro Nursing School Leads A.I. Integration
stories.summary: UNCG's School of Nursing has appointed A.I. Champions to integrate artificial intelligence across curriculum, simulation, and faculty training, according to UNC Greensboro. Seventy percent of faculty are actively using A.I. tools to enhance student engagement and support different learning styles.

stories.headline: George Washington Professor Redesigns Marketing Courses for A.I. Era
stories.summary: GW Professor Michael Tadesse has restructured his marketing courses around an "innovation mindset lab" where students work with real businesses to build A.I.-enabled prototypes, according to GW Today. His approach emphasizes strategic thinking and adaptation over traditional content delivery.

stories.headline: No-Code A.I. Tools Expand Access for Academic Users
stories.summary: New analysis highlights how no-code A.I. platforms enable students and faculty to leverage artificial intelligence without programming expertise, according to Open Source For You. Tools range from Google Teachable Machine for beginners to research assistants for literature review.
